title.narrative: • NIHR Global Health Research Short Placement Award for Research Collaboration R4 (2023)

description.narrative: Literature has it that participation of children and young people in research and interventions is low. Nevertheless, success of interventions relies on participation of the ones whom the intervention is targeting from planning to implementation. It is important then to ensure young people participate in interventions. Since participation promotion in children is quite a new concept, compared to community participation; activities and methods of promoting participation are not obvious and not always well reported by intervention implementers who reports presence of participation in their interventions. Currently, I am undertaking a PhD studentship through the NIHR Global Research Group on improving adolescent health & well-being in Malawi. I am working within work strand 4 which is exploring the role of Water Sanitation & Hygiene (WASH) on adolescent health and well-being. We are to co-design a number of WASH interventions and pilot them with the aim of recommending long-term, effective strategies to the Government. My role requires me to support the development of adolescent targeted interventions, implementation and evaluation. My PhD concept is also leaning towards promoting adolescent participation in WASH interventions. I don’t have experience in promoting participation of children and young people in research and projects. Hence the main aim of this placement is to gain knowledge and skills in that area. The placement will allow me to obtain the knowledge and practical experience in co-designing of interventions with beneficiaries and stakeholders. I will also know new people, build new networks and get some career mentorship. These will be achieved through being engaged in various projects with engagement and involvement concepts targeting children and young people. I will also attend formal training at University of Exeter through their offered short courses in line with my capacity gaps.
